headline: College teacher dies of dengue in Narsingdi at 32 years old
summary: Mosaddek Hasan, an ICT lecturer at Narsingdi Model College, passed away at the district hospital. He was admitted days earlier, and his death followed a sudden high fever and suspected stroke.
details: Mosaddek Hasan, a 32-year-old college teacher, tragically died from dengue fever in Narsingdi. He was an Information and Communication Technology (ICT) lecturer at Narsingdi Model College.

His death occurred on Friday afternoon at the Narsingdi 100-bed District Hospital, where he had been receiving treatment. Hospital superintendent Dr. Md. Mizanur Rahman confirmed he was dengue positive.

According to Dr. Rahman, Mosaddek was admitted a few days prior. On Friday, he had prayed and felt somewhat better, but later developed a severe high temperature, which may have led to a stroke and his subsequent passing.
Mosaddek Hasan was the son of Mosharraf Hossain, a teacher at Khilpara Dakhil Madrasa in Palash Upazila's Danga Union.

headline: Durga Puja begins with President and PM sending greetings of harmony
summary: Bangladesh's largest Hindu festival, Durga Puja, has officially commenced. President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman extended greetings, emphasizing religious freedom and communal harmony.
details: The main formalities of Durga Puja, the largest religious festival for Bangladeshi Hindus, began today with Kalparambha and Bihit Puja. President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman issued messages of harmony on the occasion.

Both leaders emphasized the importance of creating a safe environment for all citizens to practice their religious rituals. They reiterated their commitment to ensuring such an atmosphere across the country.
The festival, which started with Sashti, will continue for five days, concluding with the immersion of Goddess Durga's idols on Bijaya Dashami next Wednesday.

President Fakhrul stated that Durga Puja's underlying message is the destruction of evil forces and the triumph of truth, beauty, and welfare. He highlighted its embodiment of justice and humanity, and its deep intertwining with Bengal's social culture.

Prime Minister Tarique affirmed that equality, human dignity, and social justice are fundamental to all religions. He stressed the importance of mutual respect and compassion to maintain peace in society.

The Prime Minister also noted Bangladesh's democratic journey post-political changeover, committing to a safe and humane Bangladesh for all citizens, regardless of party, opinion, religion, or caste. He urged the Hindu community to celebrate peacefully and safely.
caption:
Durga Puja, Bangladesh's largest Hindu festival, has officially begun! President and Prime Minister send messages of harmony, emphasizing religious freedom for all.

The main formalities of Durga Puja, the largest religious festival for Bangladeshi Hindus, began today with Kalparambha and Bihit Puja. President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman issued messages of harmony on the occasion.

Both leaders emphasized the importance of creating a safe environment for all citizens to practice their religious rituals. They reiterated their commitment to ensuring such an atmosphere across the country.

The festival, which started with Sashti, will continue for five days, concluding with the immersion of Goddess Durga's idols on Bijaya Dashami next Wednesday.

President Fakhrul stated that Durga Puja's underlying message is the destruction of evil forces and the triumph of truth, beauty, and welfare. He highlighted its embodiment of justice and humanity, and its deep intertwining with Bengal's social culture.

Prime Minister Tarique affirmed that equality, human dignity, and social justice are fundamental to all religions. He stressed the importance of mutual respect and compassion to maintain peace in society.

The Prime Minister also noted Bangladesh's democratic journey post-political changeover, committing to a safe and humane Bangladesh for all citizens, regardless of party, opinion, religion, or caste. He urged the Hindu community to celebrate peacefully and safely.
